metadata.title: Symmetric blind information reconciliation for quantum key distribution

extraction_notes.note: Both the binary-entropy equation and the efficiency equation carry \label{eq:ffix}; the later \ref (Sec. 2.1, 'fixed by the dimension of the parity-check matrix') clearly means the efficiency formula but resolves to the entropy equation.

Appendix B has typos: $r_\mathrm{k}$ is said to use $\epsilon_\mathrm{est}$ (meaning $q_\mathrm{est}$), $A_i$ is called a set of symbol nodes (meaning check nodes), $\mathcal{N}$ is reused for the averaging window, and sentences end without periods, which constrained step boundaries.

The definition of untainted puncturing is stated only inside the leakage argument; per step rule 4/5 it stays inside a proof step rather than becoming a definition node, though Secs. 2.1-3 and App. B rely on it.
theorem or claim: a cited simulation finding ('it was shown that gradual disclosing lowers f and FER'); typed theorem/external per the rule for cited prior results stated in full.
Appendix C has no proof environment; the whole argument after the leakage statement is taken as one prose proof of ClP9 and also of the Sec. 3 security claim that defers to Appendix C.

Discussion paragraphs (shortcomings, large block lengths, QBER estimation in the Gisin setup, QSDC comparison) and figure captions with simulation results were left out as commentary without separately stated results.

nodes.statement: We note that short-length LDPC codes have been used to show the results of our method. The fact is that a small block length leads to high fluctuations in the actual number of discrepancies in raw keys even in the case of a constant QBER. In turn, these fluctuations are crucial for successful belief-propagation decoding. The feature of blind reconciliation is that it can treat fluctuations by disclosing an adequate amount of information via public channel.

nodes.statement: As a stopping criterion, we consider behavior of averaged magnitude LLRs for symbols in nonshortened positions: hatr^(k):=frac1n-ssum_iin Kcup P|r^(k)[i]|. We stop the decoding and return ``none'' as the decoded vector if, for the current step k, the following inequality holds: hatr^(k)leqfrac1Nsum_j=k-N^k-1hatr^(j), where we use N:=5. It can be interpreted as the end of a growth trend as far as our confidence in bit values. The algorithm also returns a D that is a list of d positions of symbols which has minimal values of LLR magnitude D = \i\;|\;|r^(k)[i]|leq |r^(k)[j]| ~forall jnotin D \, |D| = d. Otherwise, the algorithm goes to the next step.

nodes.statement: It is important to note that the most computationally expensive calculation~() can be optimized by using a technique suggested in Ref.. We also point out that Eq.~() reveals some peculiarity regarding punctured symbols. A zero LLR of the punctured symbol iin B_j on the first step ``deactivates'' the jth check node making all messages M_i'leftarrow j (i'in B_j, i'neq i) to other symbol nodes to be zero. If there are no punctured bits in B_j/i, then |M_ileftarrow j|>0, and the ith node is ``rescued'' after the first iteration and then participates in the decoding procedure. However, if there are at least two punctured nodes connected to a given jth check node, then all messages M_ileftarrow j, iin B_j are zero. There still a possibility that the punctures symbols will be 'rescued' via another check nodes, but such behavior nonetheless indicates the importance of choosing a set of punctured symbols. To avoid this situation the special technique of untainted puncturing is used.
nodes.raw_latex:
It is important to note that the most computationally expensive calculation~(\ref{eq:Mes}) can be optimized by using a technique suggested in Ref.~\cite{Decodoptim}.
We also point out that Eq.~(\ref{eq:Mes}) reveals some peculiarity regarding punctured symbols.
A zero LLR of the punctured symbol $i\in B_j$ on the first step ``deactivates'' the $j$th check node making all messages $\mathbf{M}_{i'\leftarrow j}$ ($i'\in B_j$, $i'\neq i$) to other symbol nodes to be zero.
If there are no punctured bits in $B_j/i$, then $|\mathbf{M}_{i\leftarrow j}|>0$, and the $i$th node is ``rescued'' after the first iteration and then participates in the decoding procedure. 
However, if there are at least two punctured nodes connected to a given $j$th check node, then all messages $\mathbf{M}_{i\leftarrow j}, i\in B_j$ are zero.
There still a possibility that the punctures symbols will be 'rescued' via another check nodes, but such behavior nonetheless indicates the importance of choosing a set of punctured symbols.
To avoid this situation the special technique of untainted puncturing is used~\cite{UntP}.
